**TL;DR**: Root cause found and proven with instrumented builds. opencode's v2 event system (when `OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL=true`) passes tool args by reference into Immer's `produce()`, which calls `Object.freeze()` on the original args object. Any plugin that mutates args in `tool.execute.before` then crashes. One-line fix in [PR #25867](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/25867). @ouchxp thanks for linking the issue and pointing to [oh-my-openagent#3816](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/3816), it helped confirm the 8 mutation sites on the plugin side. > Our earlier analysis incorrectly blamed minify and effect versions. The actual confounder was `OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL=true` set in our shell environment, which silently enabled the v2 event system for all our test runs. Once we identified the flag, the root cause became clear and provable. --- ### Workarounds (any one works) | Workaround | How | |------------|-----| | Disable experimental features | **`unset OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL`** or **`OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL=false`** | | Use pure mode | `OPENCODE_PURE=1 opencode` | | Downgrade | opencode v1.14.33 | | Remove oh-my-openagent | Remove from `"plugin"` array in config | > **Note**: Setting `OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_EVENT_SYSTEM=false` alone does NOT work if `OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL=true` is also set. The [flag resolution](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/7ded0ec9e91f62e3f0fa9c0d058ac6e86cdb4cd8/packages/core/src/flag/flag.ts#L98) uses `OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL || truthy("OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_EVENT_SYSTEM")` — the parent flag overrides the specific flag. ### Fix [PR #25867](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/25867) (updated, single commit on latest `dev`): ```diff // packages/opencode/src/session/processor.ts:329 - input: value.input, + input: structuredClone(value.input), ``` Clones the tool input before passing it to `EventV2.run`, so Immer freezes the clone instead of the original args object. ---
Detailed root cause analysis ### The bug When `OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL=true`, every tool call crashes with `TypeError: Attempted to assign to readonly property` if a plugin mutates `output.args` in a `tool.execute.before` hook. ### Exact causal chain 1. LLM makes a tool call. The AI SDK creates an `args` object from the parsed JSON. 2. The `tool-call` stream event fires in [`processor.ts:325-335`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/7ded0ec9e91f62e3f0fa9c0d058ac6e86cdb4cd8/packages/opencode/src/session/processor.ts#L325-L335). It calls `EventV2.run(SessionEvent.Tool.Called.Sync, { ..., input: value.input })` where `value.input` is the **same object reference** as the tool's `args`. 3. [`EventV2.run`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/7ded0ec9e91f62e3f0fa9c0d058ac6e86cdb4cd8/packages/opencode/src/v2/event.ts#L49-L50) checks [`Flag.OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_EVENT_SYSTEM`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/7ded0ec9e91f62e3f0fa9c0d058ac6e86cdb4cd8/packages/core/src/flag/flag.ts#L98) (inherits from `OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL`). When the flag is **on**, it calls `SyncEvent.run(def, data)`. 4. `SyncEvent.run` routes through the projector to [`SessionMessageUpdater`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/7ded0ec9e91f62e3f0fa9c0d058ac6e86cdb4cd8/packages/opencode/src/v2/session-message-updater.ts#L276-L289), which uses [Immer `produce()`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/7ded0ec9e91f62e3f0fa9c0d058ac6e86cdb4cd8/packages/opencode/src/v2/session-message-updater.ts#L1) to update the assistant message state. Inside the draft, it stores [`event.data.input`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/7ded0ec9e91f62e3f0fa9c0d058ac6e86cdb4cd8/packages/opencode/src/v2/session-message-updater.ts#L283) (the same reference as `args`). 5. **Immer's `produce()` calls `Object.freeze()` on the entire produced state tree**, including the `args` object that was stored by reference. 6. @rekram1-node Well, in this (hopefully rare) case, the bug is in the (new experimental) event system and the plugins (currently) still rely on getting **mutable arguments** (like a tool command). This (implicit) contract of having mutable arguments will be broken on release of the new event system, and will break a lot of plugins. `OPENCODE_PURE=0` "fixes" the issue but the root cause is a change in the contract/interface between `opencode` and its plugins. I don't think this is communicated or written down at all. The question is should `opencode` drop the `immer` freeze of arguments to keep the implicit functionality, or should it keep frozen args but then make plugin devs aware of it.

**Correction to my previous comments here**: the root cause is NOT minify, NOT effect versions, NOT Bun JSC behavior. Those were red herrings caused by `OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL=true` being set in our test environment, which silently enabled the v2 event system for all our builds.

**Actual root cause**: The v2 event system ([PR #24512](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/24512)) passes tool args by reference into Immer's `produce()` via [`processor.ts:329`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/7ded0ec9e91f62e3f0fa9c0d058ac6e86cdb4cd8/packages/opencode/src/session/processor.ts#L329). Immer calls `Object.freeze()` on the produced state tree, which freezes the original `args` object. Plugin hooks that mutate `args` then throw `TypeError: Attempted to assign to readonly property`.

**Affected users**: Those with `OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL=true` AND a plugin that mutates tool args (e.g. oh-my-openagent).

**Workaround**: **`unset OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL`** or **`OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL=false`**.

> **Note**: Setting `OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_EVENT_SYSTEM=false` alone does NOT work if `OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL=true` is also set. The [flag resolution](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/7ded0ec9e91f62e3f0fa9c0d058ac6e86cdb4cd8/packages/core/src/flag/flag.ts#L98) uses `OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL || truthy(...)` — the parent flag overrides the specific flag.

**Fix**: [PR #25867](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/25867) (1 line: `structuredClone(value.input)` before passing to EventV2).

Full details in [#25873](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/25873).

I tracked this down to the npm wrapper at `packages/opencode/bin/opencode`, not the `serve` implementation itself.

The wrapper uses blocking `spawnSync()` around the real `.opencode` binary. When a supervisor sends `SIGTERM` to the wrapper, the wrapper dies without forwarding the signal and the real `.opencode serve` child is reparented to PID 1.

I opened a fix here: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/26259

Hard A/B evidence with `homeboy observe`:

| Case | Homeboy run | Result |
|---|---:|---|
| Stock upstream wrapper | `8d26c4f6-4e90-459b-a15d-49e76cc0f9da` | **3/3 orphans** |
| Patched wrapper from PR #26259 | `bdc45e95-2ec3-44bf-b50a-c7daee37552e` | **0/3 orphans** |

Signals tested in both cases:

- `SIGTERM`
- `SIGINT`
- `SIGHUP`

So this is a simple wrapper fix: replace `spawnSync()` with async `spawn()`, forward termination signals to the child, and preserve signal-based exit semantics.

I opened a PR that fixes this wrapper path as part of the same root cause: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/26259

The current wrapper has two related signal bugs:

1. It uses blocking `spawnSync()`, so the wrapper cannot forward `SIGTERM`/`SIGINT`/`SIGHUP` while the child is running. If a supervisor kills the wrapper, the real `.opencode` child can survive and become a PID-1 orphan.
2. As this issue notes, `spawnSync()` reports signal exits as `status: null` with `signal` set, and the wrapper currently maps that to exit code `0`.

The PR switches to async `spawn()`, forwards standard termination signals to the child, and when the child exits due to a signal, re-raises that signal on the wrapper process instead of converting it to `0`.

Verification:

| Case | Homeboy run | Result |
|---|---:|---|
| Stock upstream wrapper | `8d26c4f6-4e90-459b-a15d-49e76cc0f9da` | **3/3 orphans** |
| Patched wrapper from PR #26259 | `bdc45e95-2ec3-44bf-b50a-c7daee37552e` | **0/3 orphans** |

Signals tested: `SIGTERM`, `SIGINT`, `SIGHUP`.

Hi team, regarding this issue, I'd like to propose a potential solution that might improve the experience for users dealing with various custom proxies:

Add a "Provider Type / API Protocol" dropdown in the Custom Provider UI

Instead of hardcoding and defaulting to @ai-sdk/openai-compatible when creating a custom provider, it would be incredibly helpful to have a dropdown menu where users can explicitly select the underlying API protocol or SDK.

Options could include: OpenAI Compatible (as default), Google / Gemini, Anthropic, Mistral, etc.
Benefits: This is the most straightforward approach and would perfectly resolve compatibility issues for users connecting through enterprise internal proxies or custom API gateways that don't use the OpenAI format.
Hope this suggestion is helpful! Thanks for the great work on OpenCode.

I have dig into this issue and find it's more like a build-dist problem.

# reproduce

```bash
curl -X GET 'https://opencode.ai/docs/pagefind/pagefind.js' \
  --header 'User-Agent: yaak' \
  --header 'Accept: */*' \
  --header 'Cookie: oc_locale=en'
```

It works. 

And if you change `oc_locale` to any other locale it'll break down. like:

```bash
curl -X GET 'https://opencode.ai/docs/pagefind/pagefind.js' \
  --header 'User-Agent: yaak' \
  --header 'Accept: */*' \
  --header 'Cookie: oc_locale=de'
```

# Why

- run `bun --cwd packages/web build` and check the folder `packages/web/dist/docs`

Apparently, there is indeed exsit `pagefind` folder and `pagefind.js`. But with locales, each locale has its own root, and there is no `pagefind` folder in locale folder.

For example, when you visit homepage on en, the `docs` is root folder.But the root folder change to `docs/de` when visit homepage on de.

> This issue might be a duplicate of existing issues. Please check:
> 
>     * [[FEATURE]: Show subagent model in session tree / subagent view #23028](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/23028): Requests showing the subagent's model in the session tree/UI — your request to also show the reasoning/variant level is closely related and may be better added as a comment there.
> 
>     * [Subtasks do not inherit the active model variant from the parent session #24757](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/24757): Subtasks not inheriting the active model variant from the parent session — related to variant/reasoning level handling in subagents.

I think this feature would be even more useful if the UI showed not only the subagent's model, but also the effective reasoning / variant / effort level being used.

For example:

- Plan — GPT-5.4 — high
  - General — GPT-5.4-mini — medium
  - Build — Sonnet-4.5 — default

Currently, when a subagent is invoked, seeing only the model name can still feel incomplete, especially for models where variants or reasoning-effort levels significantly affect behavior, latency, and cost. Displaying the effective variant/reasoning level would make subagent runs more transparent and easier to audit/debug.

This also seems related to #24757, where subtasks may not inherit the active model variant from the parent session. Even after inheritance/configuration behavior is fixed, showing the effective variant in the session tree or subagent view would help users verify what is actually being used at runtime.

- For a session ID returned by the CLI:
  - `session_info(session_id)` succeeds and reports message count/date range/transcript metadata.
  - `session_read(session_id)` fails with `Session not found`.
- `session_search(...)` also returns no matches for terms present in the active session context.
- The legacy session storage directory (`~/.local/share/opencode/storage/session/`) exists but contains `0` entries.
- `opencode db path` points to the SQLite DB under the normal OpenCode data directory.

This looks like the session tools and the CLI/runtime are not reading the same source of truth. The CLI sees sessions in the current SQLite-backed store, while `session_list`/`session_read` appear to miss them, possibly by consulting legacy file storage or applying a different project/session filter.
